full_judgment:
2. The decree-holder respondents instituted Title Suit No. 221 of 1987 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla for permanent injunction against the petitioners for restraining them from construction of a building on the allegations, inter alia, that they were in possession of the building described in the first schedule of the plaint as owners and that the properties described in the second schedule of the plaint were owned by the petitioners. The properties described in both the schedules are situated in Bagichagaon, Comilla. The respondents alleged that the construction made by the petitioners on the land adjacent to the building of the respondents violated the Building Construction Act, 1952 as it created obstruction to the enjoyment of light and air by the respondents and affected the privacy of the members of their family. The petitioners did not keep a vacant space of 10 feet at the back and 4 feet on both the sides of the building, as required by the said Act. The respondents also complained to the Chairman of Comilla Paurashava sensing his interference in such illegal construction. The Chairman after holding enquiry restrained the petitioners from continuing construction violating the approved plan. But the petitioners did not comply with the direction of the Chairman Hence this suit. 

 3. The petitioners contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable, that they were constructing according to the approved plan and not illegally as alleged by the respondents. The trial Court decreed the suit against the petitioners and restrained them from making any construction without keeping 10 feet space in the back side and 4 feet on both sides of the building and passed a mandatory injunction directing the demolition of the constructions made by encroachment on the vacant spaces. The petitioners took appeal to the District Judge being Title Appeal No. 158 of 1989. The appeal was decreed on 13-1-1990 in terms of a compromise. One of the terms of the compromise was that the parties shall adhere to the terms of compromise failing which the respondents would execute the decree passed by the trial Court otherwise the decree shall be inoperative. 

 4. As the petitioners did not comply with the terms of compromise decree the respondents put trial Court's decree in execution in Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1991 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Comilla. 

 6. Dr Ahmed Hussain, learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the High Court Division misconstruing the terms of compromise decree erroneously held that the petitioners have admitted some unauthorized construction on the second schedule land in spite of the fact they sought for an appointment of an engineer to ascertain the extent of the unauthorized construction. He further submits that the High Court Division upon misinterpretation of the compromise decree acted illegally in not holding that the executing Court committed an error of law in rejecting the petitions of the petitioners resulting in an error in decision occasioning failure of justice. Lastly, he submits that the point involved in the case is of public interest inasmuch as it seeks to determine the scope of revisional application under section 115 CPC. 

 7. Reading the impugned judgment it appears that the High Court Division found that the petitioners admitted some unauthorized construction on the second schedule land and the respondents prayed for appointment of a Magistrate, police personnel’s and an engineer for the purpose of demolition of the unauthorized construction of the building pursuant to the compromise decree. The High Court Division also noticed that the petitioners also prayed for appointment of an engineer for ascertainment of the extent of unauthorized construction. It observed that the engineer to be appointed by the Court on the application of the respondents is quite competent to ascertain the extent of unauthorized construction in question and no other engineer as sought to be appointed by the petitioners is necessary. It further held that the executing Court will execute only the decree and it has no jurisdiction to go beyond the decree i.e. beyond the compromise decree wherein the rights of the parties were conclusively determined by the Court and the executing Court for executing the decree cannot enter into the merit of the decree.
